gaps.gap: It is unresolved whether prompt optimizers actually gain anything from being coupled to an external episodic memory or experience store, because the methods that optimize prompts do so without any memory bank and the one paper that does couple memory with optimization studies interaction only inside its own closed loop.
gaps.evidence_needed: A controlled comparison running the same prompt optimizer with and without an attached episodic memory/experience store on the same tasks, models, and budget, reporting the isolated contribution of the memory component.

gaps.gap: How the memory retrieval mechanism inside a coupled optimizer affects the optimization outcome is untested, since the only system that reports cross-task interference attributes it to lexical Jaccard retrieval and merely recommends dense retrieval without evaluating it, while pipeline-level and codebook-level alternatives change the retrieval/selection unit without isolating this factor.
gaps.evidence_needed: An ablation holding the optimizer fixed and swapping only the retrieval mechanism (Jaccard word-overlap vs. dense sentence-embedding retrieval vs. task-type-filtered retrieval), measuring cross-task interference and final accuracy per condition.

gaps.gap: Whether the reported gains and the variance amplification of coupled multi-component optimizers survive across model families and scales is unresolved, as each method validates on a narrow and non-overlapping model set and explicitly defers broader validation.
gaps.evidence_needed: Multi-model replication of the same optimizers across families and scales (e.g., GPT-4o, Mistral-7B, and models beyond 8B) with multiple seeds, reporting both mean gain and variance per model.

gaps.gap: It is unresolved whether optimization is worth running at all relative to a well-designed fixed scaffold, and whether coupled optimizers add anything when started from an already-strong initialization, since the one paper that measures this finds fixed prompts winning in low-data regimes and leaves strong-scaffold initialization open while other methods report gains only against zero-shot or weak baselines.
gaps.evidence_needed: A sweep over training-set size and initialization quality (zero-init vs. CoT-zero/CoT-math or other strong fixed scaffolds) showing the crossover point at which optimized prompts beat the best fixed scaffold.

gaps.gap: The optimization signals used for coupled prompt refinement are of unverified validity, because scoring depends on automatic metrics without human judgment in one case and on self-generated retry traces whose dependence on the generating model is untested in another, while several methods report no benchmark, model, or numeric detail at all.
gaps.evidence_needed: Human evaluation of optimized outputs on open-ended tasks alongside the automatic metrics, plus generation of the contrastive retry traces with multiple different models to test whether the extracted rules transfer or are generator-specific, reported with named benchmarks and headline numbers.

gaps.gap: It is unresolved whether the headline gains claimed for memory and evolution systems survive run-to-run stochasticity, since several papers report single point-estimate percentage improvements with no variance or significance testing while the papers that do measure variance show it can be amplified several-fold by the very design choices that raise the mean (candidate-pool size) and that three runs per cell supports only paradigm-level, not per-condition, conclusions.
gaps.evidence_needed: Re-running the same memory conditions over many seeds and reporting the full per-seed distribution with paired significance tests (as done for the MAGE-vs-GEPA and holistic-vs-atomic-judge comparisons) would show which reported deltas exceed seed noise.

gaps.gap: Whether memory-system gains are worth their compute is unresolved, because the construction, maintenance, and meta-search costs of the more elaborate designs (hypergraph building and pruning, meta-evolution over architectures, iterative pipeline evolution) are not reported alongside their accuracy gains, so no comparison is made at matched budget against a fixed heuristic memory.
gaps.evidence_needed: Budget-matched comparisons that hold tokens, wall-clock latency, and dollar cost fixed across substrates and report accuracy as a function of that budget — the efficiency instrumentation the unified-harness study describes but has not released — would settle whether the elaborate designs dominate simple ones per unit of compute.

gaps.gap: The number of memory items injected per query is treated as an unreported implementation detail rather than an experimental variable, so it is unknown how much of any reported gain or harm is attributable to injection dose rather than to memory structure, even though separate evidence shows broad retrieval helps factual QA while hurting sequential decision-making and that repeated exposure to conflicting memory amplifies failure.
gaps.evidence_needed: A dose-response sweep varying only the number of retrieved items per query within a fixed substrate and backbone, reporting task success and conflicting-memory compliance jointly across both QA and decision-making suites, would separate the effect of injection budget from that of memory structure.

gaps.gap: The instruments used to score memory experiments — LLM judges, automatic ability/skill extractors, and noise-injection pipelines — are themselves largely unvalidated in the memory setting, since judge behavior is shown to be highly sensitive to reference quality but never tested in interaction with a memory system, extraction vocabulary reflects a single extractor's idiosyncrasies, one robustness framework reports no benchmarks, models, or numbers at all, and process-aware multi-view evaluation has been demonstrated only where no memory mechanism is present.
gaps.evidence_needed: Holding a human-annotated ground truth fixed while varying the judge design, the ability extractor, and the noise level, and checking whether the induced ranking of memory conditions changes, would establish whether current memory results are artifacts of the measurement instrument.

gaps.gap: Evaluation horizons are too short to test the consolidation claims memory systems are built on: durability of distilled skills past a single frozen deployment phase, stability of evolved pipelines over many more iterations, and substrate behavior at long histories are all left untested, even though the substrate study already observes that designs effective at moderate history lengths become costly or brittle at longer ones and the survey names cross-task consolidation as the central open challenge.
gaps.evidence_needed: Longitudinal runs that extend the same agent and memory store across many task episodes and evolution iterations, reporting accuracy, retrieval quality, and store size over time rather than at a single endpoint, would show whether apparent consolidation gains persist, plateau, or degrade into clutter.

gaps.gap: No study isolates how much of a memory system's gain comes from the write/consolidation policy (what is extracted, structured, and pruned) versus the retrieval mechanism that surfaces it, so reported improvements cannot be attributed to memory structure itself.
gaps.evidence_needed: A factorial ablation holding one factor fixed while varying the other — same write/consolidation policy across two or more retrieval mechanisms and the same retriever across two or more write policies, on shared benchmarks and backbones with per-cell deltas.

gaps.gap: It is unresolved whether distilling episodic traces into abstracted units (skills, four-field records, workflow/subtask hierarchies, Abilities) actually beats reusing raw trajectories, since cards report directly conflicting outcomes and none tests which contextual cues abstraction discards.
gaps.evidence_needed: A controlled comparison of raw-trajectory reuse against multiple abstraction levels under a matched token budget, across task families that differ in context shift and composition demands, with error analysis attributing failures to information lost in distillation.

gaps.gap: The claim that memory management should become learnable or decision-theoretic rather than hand-designed heuristic remains empirically ungrounded, and the compute/latency overhead such adaptive write policies impose is not measured against the fixed heuristics they aim to replace.
gaps.evidence_needed: Head-to-head runs of learned/evolved memory-management policies against strong heuristic baselines on the same benchmarks, reporting both task accuracy and the full cost of construction, maintenance, and periodic refinement (LLM calls, tokens, wall-clock) at matched budgets.

gaps.gap: Whether memory write policy and prompt/instruction optimization interact — reinforcing, substituting for, or destabilizing each other — is untested, even though one card reports that stochastic optimization signals inside a closed reflective loop couple in ways not predictable from components in isolation.
gaps.evidence_needed: A crossed design running memory evolution with and without prompt optimization (and from weak versus already-strong fixed scaffolds) over multiple seeds, reporting the interaction term in both mean performance and variance rather than each component's solo gain.

gaps.gap: Reported write-policy gains are not shown to survive changes of backbone, model scale, or memory substrate, and are often stated without variance or significance, so it is unclear whether any structure choice generalizes or merely fits one operating regime.
gaps.evidence_needed: Multi-backbone, multi-scale replications of the same write policy under one unified harness with multiple seeds and reported variance/significance, including parametric versus retrieval-based substrates and long-horizon regimes where substrate effectiveness is said to invert.

gaps.gap: Across systems whose gains are attributed to memory, no card isolates how much of the improvement comes from the write/consolidation policy versus the retrieval mechanism that surfaces those memories at query time, so the causal locus of the reported gains is unresolved.
gaps.evidence_needed: A factorial ablation that crosses each write/consolidation policy with a fixed common retriever and each retrieval mechanism with a fixed common memory pool, on the same benchmarks and backbones, reporting per-cell task performance.

gaps.gap: Memory content is increasingly made adaptive or learned while the retrieval step stays a predefined similarity/top-k procedure, and no card establishes whether a learned or corpus-aware retriever would add anything on top of adaptive memory content in an agent setting.
gaps.evidence_needed: A head-to-head comparison, within one agent memory system, of fixed dense top-k against learned and jointly-decoded retrieval (e.g. NNN-style) over the same memory store, reporting both task success and the retrieval compute/latency cost.

gaps.gap: The size of the injection budget — how many memory items are read, used, or proactively placed in context per query — is unmeasured as a controlled variable, so the shape of the accuracy-versus-tokens tradeoff and the point at which more injected memory stops helping are unknown.
gaps.evidence_needed: A sweep over the number and token volume of injected memory items (and over proactive versus reactive placement) at fixed retriever and memory pool, reporting task performance and context-token consumption per setting.

gaps.gap: Retrieved memory can actively harm agents — by shifting attention away from action-critical context in sequential decision-making, and by inducing compliance with conflicting entries from which agents rarely recover — but no card tests an admission, gating, or routing policy that decides when to retrieve or inject at all.
gaps.evidence_needed: Controlled experiments in which a gating or substrate-routing policy is switched on and off against always-retrieve and never-retrieve baselines, on both long-context QA and sequential decision-making tasks, measuring entry-level compliance with bad memories alongside end-task success.

gaps.gap: Retrieval and injection results are reported under narrow and non-overlapping conditions — single backbones, single benchmark families, no variance reporting — so it is unresolved whether any retrieval mechanism's advantage survives a change of backbone, task domain, or horizon length.
gaps.evidence_needed: Evaluation of the same retrieval/injection configurations across multiple backbones and several benchmark suites under one unified harness, with repeated runs reporting variance or significance tests and results broken out by interaction-history length.
